Show HN: Enso Method – agent skills for building software for someone else
items.summary: The Enso Method is a new set of AI skills for Claude Code and Codex which I've open sourced on GitHub predominantly for developers who build for someone else who is making the product/business calls. I've been using AI to write basically 100% of my code since late 2024, back in the Sonnet 3.5 days, when it barely worked and there were few people doing this and very little support for this way of developing. I stubbornly thought this was going to be the future and came up with a methodology for making it work, before "AI skills" were even a thing. Since then I've continued to refine the method and I just recently published it as open source. The method focuses on requirements (PRD, TDD) up front, and has skills that autonomously refine the requirements, declaring assumptions that should be validated by stakeholders. It doesn't expect you to be a solo founder or that whoever is at the keyboard directing Claude or Codex to be the product owner and business decider in addition to being the developer. I think most of us sit in the seat where we develop for someone else who decides. And if AI is all about velocity, then if we have to slow down to get product owners to review and decide, that puts a serious damper on the efficiency everyone expects from AI development. So a defining attribute of the Enso Method is, when it reviews the requirements prior to implementation, it asks what questions/gaps there are and it tries to answer its own questions. If it can get to 95%+ confidence in the answers, it just rolls with those. If less then it will declare the assumption in an assumptions.md file which gets routed to business stakeholders to review. In the meantime however we still consider this to be a green light, we can move forward and implement with the assumptions, and if we later hear from the business that the assumption was wrong, we update the requirements and re-implement, because implementation is now cheap, and waiting isn't.

items.title: Show HN: E2E – Open-source agentic testing framework for web, iOS and Android
items.summary: Hey HN, I’m Oskar, one of the co-founders of TesterArmy. We built an agentic testing framework for web and mobile because traditional testing frameworks can’t keep up with the pace of how we build software today. e2e allows you to mix deterministic and agentic APIs in the same test. You can write the test cases using familiar APIs like `getByText()`or `getByTestId()` which you can also mix it with agentic `agent.act()`. The unique part about it is that e2e will cache and replay the agentic actions so you don’t have to pay for AI on each run. You can use it with any LLM, including subscriptions you are already paying for. On top of that, the core of e2e is platform agnostic. We ship both web and mobile engines out of the box; adding support for more platforms is pretty straightforward. Here’s a code short code snippet of an example test: ```ts import { test, expect } from 'e2e'; test('a member upgrades to Pro', async ({ app, agent, screen }) => { await app.open('/settings/billing'); await agent.act('upgrade the workspace to the Pro plan'); await agent.assert('the invoice preview shows a prorated amount'); await expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toContainText('Pro'); }); ``` Try it: npx e2e init GitHub: https://github.com/tester-army/e2e

items.title: Show HN: Baa – a menu bar app that frees RAM your AI agents forgot about
items.summary: i built this because my mac keeps running out of RAM every 2 hours and i typically get around it by closing random apps and hoping it will help. :') baa sits in the menu bar and: - finds stuff still eating memory after its app or terminal closed, or that ai agents started and forgot (dev servers, headless browsers) - shows how much you'd get back and frees it in one click - warns you a few minutes before you run out - also finds dev junk on your disk (old builds, package caches etc.) open source and nothing leaves your machine. would love feedback! baa would've cleared ~50gb on my mac :)
